title: God gave the increase (1 Corinthians 3:5–9)

lines: I'M WITH PAUL. I'M WITH APOLLOS.
cards: Remember Apollos? Eighteen days ago, Priscilla and Aquila took him aside in Ephesus and taught him the way of God more perfectly.

Then he crossed to Achaia, Corinth's province, and Acts says he was a great help to the believers there. By the time Paul writes this letter, the church in Corinth has split into fan clubs. I'm with Paul.
I'm with Apollos. I'm with Cephas, that is, Peter. And, I'm with Christ.
Parishes, teams and families still split this way over favorite people.

teach.h: WHO IS PAUL? WHO IS APOLLOS?
teach.b: Paul could have used this moment to win; he was the founder. Instead he deflates the whole contest, himself included. Who is Paul, and who is Apollos?

Servants, through whom you believed, each doing what the Lord gave him. Then a farmer's picture, in the Douay-Rheims, which spells the name Apollo: "I have planted, Apollo watered, but God gave the increase."
Paul put the seed in the ground in Corinth. Apollos came later with the watering can. Both mattered.
But neither can make a seed grow; you can only set things up and wait. So: "Therefore, neither he that planteth is any thing, nor he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase."
Humbling for the well-known preacher, freeing for everyone else.

He who plants and he who waters are one, and each will receive his own reward according to his own labor. Then: "For we are God's coadjutors: you are God's husbandry; you are God's building." Coadjutors means co-workers.
Husbandry here means a farm, a field under cultivation. The Corinthians aren't anyone's fan club. They're God's field.
Notice how gently Paul treats Apollos: not a rival, a co-worker. And notice the honest limit of every worker's job.
You can't make your kids believe, your friend heal, your project take off, or your parish grow.
You plant, you water, and the increase belongs to God.
Catholics reach for this line when their part seems small.

how: Catholics speak of many vocations and gifts serving one Church, priests, religious, catechists, parents and parishioners each with a part, and they pray for growth that they believe comes from God alone.

o: farmers who own the field outright

games.q: the field at Corinth — tap the pairs.
p: a farm, a field under cultivation

s: Paul calls them servants and co-workers: one plants, one waters.
the Corinthians split into groups around favorite leaders
I'm with Paul, I'm with Apollos, I'm with Peter, I'm with Christ.
Paul says whoever plants is the one who matters most
neither the planter nor the waterer is anything; God gives the increase.

games.q: you're Paul, the founder. your church has split, and some prefer the newer, more eloquent preacher. what do you do?
o: remind them you founded the church.
call yourself and him servants, and say only God makes it grow.
games.why: he deflates the whole contest: I have planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase.

practice: Think of something you care about but can't control: a child's faith, a friend's recovery, a project at work, a parish, a garden.

Name your one small part in it, planting, watering, or simply not trampling it, and picture setting down the rest, the growing, which was never yours to do. If you pray, hand God the increase, and keep only your watering can.

wordCard.voice: Coadjutors. Paul's word for himself and Apollos: co-workers who planted and watered, while God alone gave the increase. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: made it grow, gave the increase. the verb is kept for God alone.

carryVoice: Your line: god gives the increase. Your part is the planting and the watering. Day five hundred seventy.
